overall_summary: Two movers carry a red couch across a front yard from the house doorway toward an open moving-truck ramp; just as they step onto the ramp, a red fox trots through the ramp threshold at their feet, and a bystander filming the move on their phone whips the camera toward the fox in surprise.
tone: Candid, unscripted, mildly startling then charming - real found-footage energy, not staged or comedic-timed.
capture_style: Handheld smartphone video shot by a bystander/neighbor casually filming the move, held at chest height, dusk light, mid-2000s/2011-era phone camera sensor quality - not a modern flagship phone look.
visual_style: Naturalistic UK suburban terraced street at dusk, muted overcast color grade, practical streetlight and porch-light sources only, no cinematic lighting rig.
visual_realism: Ordinary consumer phone image quality: mild motion blur on handheld movement, visible compression softness, limited dynamic range, slight sensor noise in the shadow areas, no artificial sharpening or stabilization.
audio_policy: Diegetic only - ambient street sound, footsteps, couch friction/creak, fox's paws on the pavement, the bystander's own surprised exhale/gasp.
camera_lock: UNLOCKED (v2 test) - the camera is not locked off. It reacts like a real untrained bystander: a reflexive whip-pan toward the fox's motion at the trigger moment, with natural handheld shake and a partial re-settle afterward. This is the specific behavior this test shot exists to validate.
continuity_invariants: Exactly two movers, one red couch, one red fox, and one open truck ramp appear across every frame - never duplicated, never an extra copy of any subject
The truck ramp stays open and in the same curb position in every frame

The couch's position advances measurably forward each frame along one continuous path from the house doorway to the ramp - never resets, never jumps backward, never stays visually static between consecutive frames
The fox enters from the same side it is first seen on and continues in one consistent direction of travel
Camera viewpoint is the bystander's phone the entire time - never cuts to a different capture device

Mover 1 (the front carrier, closer to the truck) walks BACKWARD facing Mover 2 for the entire shot, in every single frame - this is how two people naturally carry a couch, so they can see each other. Mover 1 never turns around and never switches to a forward-facing grip. Mover 2 (the rear carrier) walks forward facing Mover 1's back the entire time. This exact orientation is fixed starting in frame 1 and does not change in any later frame.

panel_convention: Six 16:9 landscape frames arranged in a 3-column by 2-row grid (frames 1-3 top row left to right, frames 4-6 bottom row left to right), each individual cell followed immediately by its own clean white caption band containing only the frame number and the one-sentence caption text - no text, numbers, or graphics inside the image area itself. This matches the workspace's standard Neon Parcel storyboard grid layout exactly. This is a continuity planning reference for a video model, not a comic layout to be reproduced literally.
hard_constraints: No on-screen text, logos, watermarks, or graphics inside any image area
No duplicate movers, couches, fox, or ramp in any single frame
Preserve one consistent phone-POV camera viewpoint throughout - never switch to a different capture device mid-sequence
Dusk lighting and UK suburban terraced-street setting must stay consistent across all six frames
The couch and movers must be in a visibly, measurably different position in every one of frames 1 through 4 - no two consecutive frames may show them in the same spot
Mover 1's body orientation (walking backward, facing Mover 2) must be identical in every single frame - do not let him face forward or switch grip in any frame
Do not add a caption, subtitle, or label to the couch, fox, or movers beyond the white caption band text specified per frame
